cards.front: What does a unit quaternion $q = [q_0, \mathbf{q}]$ represent in spacecraft attitude kinematics?
cards.back: A unit quaternion parameterizes a rotation in SO(3) via the axis-angle relation $q_0 = \cos(\theta/2)$, $\mathbf{q} = \sin(\theta/2)\hat{\mathbf{u}}$, free of singularities and with a double cover of the rotation group.

cards.front: State the standard quaternion kinematic equation relating $\dot{q}$ to angular velocity $\omega$.
cards.back: $\dot{q} = \frac12 \Xi(q)\omega$, where $\omega$ is the body-frame angular-velocity vector.

cards.front: Give the explicit 4×3 matrix $\Xi(q)$ used in the quaternion kinematics equation.
cards.back: $$\Xi(q) = \begin{bmatrix} -\mathbf{q}^T \\ q_0 I_3 + [\mathbf{q}\times] \end{bmatrix}$$ where $[\mathbf{q}\times]$ is the 3×3 cross-product matrix.

cards.front: Rewrite the kinematics $\dot{q} = \frac12 \Xi(q)\omega$ using quaternion multiplication.
cards.back: Equivalent form: $\dot{q} = \frac12 q \otimes \omega_q$ where $\omega_q = [0, \boldsymbol{\omega}]$ is a pure quaternion and $\otimes$ denotes Hamilton product.

cards.front: Why do quaternion kinematics avoid gimbal lock and singularities that appear with Euler angles?
cards.back: The representation is a 4-parameter double cover of SO(3) with only the unit-norm constraint; no trigonometric denominators or coordinate singularities arise.

cards.front: Derive the quaternion kinematics equation starting from the direction-cosine-matrix differential equation.
cards.back: Start with $\dot{C} = -[\omega\times]C$. Substitute the quaternion-to-DCM map $C(q)$ and differentiate; after algebraic simplification using quaternion identities the result collapses to $\dot{q} = \frac12 \Xi(q)\omega$.

cards.front: Prove that the norm of $q$ is preserved under the kinematics when $|q(0)|=1$.
cards.back: Compute $\frac{d}{dt}(q^T q) = 2q^T\dot{q} = q^T\Xi(q)\omega$. The rows of $\Xi(q)$ are orthogonal to $q$, hence $q^T\Xi(q)=0$ and $\frac{d}{dt}|q|^2=0$.

cards.front: In numerical integration of attitude, what simple correction is applied after each step to maintain $|q|=1$?
cards.back: Renormalize: $q \leftarrow q/|q|$. This is valid because the continuous kinematics already preserve the unit sphere.
